title: Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you
description: Upgrading its portfolio of 1,800 stores is high on the list of Boots' new owners, Wittington Investments. This is the holding company of the Westons -
body: Upgrading its portfolio of 1,800 stores is high on the list of Boots' new owners, Wittington Investments. This is the holding company of the Westons -  a wealthy and retail-steeped Canadian family who used to own Selfridges and currently own several large retailers across the Atlantic.  The UK branch of the family also controls the owner of Primark, Associated British Foods (ABF).What Boots stores might look like in the future has not been disclosed.Business has been good for Boots in recent years, and new-look beauty areas in some of its bigger shops have given shoppers more of a department store experience, according to Sofie Willmott, an associate director and analyst at GlobalData Retail.Since the opening of its first beauty-only store in 2023 in the Battersea Power Station development, it says it has redesigned over 180 beauty halls, while also opening its first fragrance concept store and an Opticians dedicated to luxury eyewear."They should invest in the rest of the chain because they've got such a big store portfolio that I think some of the smaller stores have really lacked investment over time, and I think that is something that they need to kind of catch up with," Willmott says.A more "consistent" look would also be an improvement, Willmott adds. "At the moment there is a bit of a disconnect."Jackie Naghten, a retail industry veteran who has worked for the likes of Top Shop, Marks & Spencer and Debenhams, thinks Boots' stores need to be made "more functional" by not having their health hubs "squeezed in the corner".But Yasmin Trimble, 22, who buys beauty products from Boots, likes how easy the stores are to navigate. "You can get everything you need...it is not confusing. It has got a cleaner aesthetic to it as well."Boots was an early adopter of the loyalty cards commonly offered today by companies offering points and discounts to customers who sign up.Its Advantage card, launched in 1997, is unlikely to go away and remains popular. Naghten doesn't think they would get rid of it. "It's the best-value store card in terms of bang for your buck."The card offers shoppers three points for every pound they spend. Each point is worth 1p.Katie Burrows, 23, is a fan of building up the points to get money off.She mainly shops at Boots for skincare, first aid and medicine, but thinks prices for its sanitary products are "ridiculously expensive" - something her friend Yasmin agrees with.Lewis Harrison believes the loyalty card is also good value, but finds it "frustrating how the rewards points only cover a full transaction"."I wish you could use your points for a partial transaction like you can in Holland and Barrett," the 25-year-old says. "It would be good to use the points towards more expensive transactions."Natalie Berg, retail expert and founder of consultancy NBK Retail, suggests the Advantage card gives Boots "a unique understanding of their customers" and is an asset the new owners "will want to double down on"."As AI and social media change how people discover and buy products, that direct relationship with customers will only become more important."The new owners have already signalled they plan to expand Boots' healthcare service, a booming industry at the moment.The retailer started out as an apothecary, so health is in its roots. Today, it offers a wide range of health and wellbeing services as well as prescriptions and vaccinations through its in-store pharmacies.It also announced earlier this summer it was expanding services for weight loss drugs, which have surged in popularity.Naghten points out that the Weston family's purchase of Boots comes at a time when pharmacies are increasingly going to prescribe more medications and health services, in a bid to ease pressure on GP surgeries and hospitals."They didn't buy this thing for no reason. They have got the blueprint," she says.While health will remain a core part of its business, Boots has other strengths, Naghten adds, in its No7 make-up and skincare products."When you have all these people coming in for health and wellbeing services, they will also be picking up a lipstick," she says.Willmott suggests Boots has an "edge" over its rivals on the health side, given its reputation as an expert.But the company is facing tough competition, which Boots acknowledged affected revenues in its latest financial results. Shoppers, particularly younger ones, are increasingly seeking products online through influencer ads rather than heading to brick-and-mortar shops. There are also other big players, such as Superdrug. And M&S this week announced a new partnership with Sephora, saying it would replace a hundred of its own beauty departments with the brand next year. For 18-year-old Schekina Bourne, Boots is not a "go-to shop" for her. "Even though I can go to Boots even in my area....Superdrug is like closest to me. So, I'll prefer the convenience," she says.Additional reporting by Ben Sturt and Anuk Weerawardana

schema.headline: Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you

title: Sara Sharif's grandfather granted guardianship of her siblings in Pakistan
description: Sara Sharif's paternal grandfather has been granted guardianship of her siblings by a court in Pakistan.The decision comes after years of legal limbo
body: Sara Sharif's paternal grandfather has been granted guardianship of her siblings by a court in Pakistan.The decision comes after years of legal limbo following the murder of 10-year-old Sara by her father and stepmother in 2023.All five children, who are now aged between 16 and four, have been living in Pakistan since 2023. They were asked to speak to the judge in court, where the eldest said they were comfortable and the siblings were settled.Sara's grandfather, Muhammed Sharif, told the BBC he was relieved to be granted guardianship after three years of legal battles, saying his hope is that the children "stay healthy" and receive "a good education"."It is my responsibility to ensure they get the best possible education and care," he said.When told by the judge that the grandfather would become their guardian, the eldest child responded saying "that's all good".The five children have been in Pakistan since August 2023, when they were brought to the country by Sara's father, stepmother and uncle after Sara was killed. The family was in hiding for weeks before the children were discovered by police at the grandfather's house. They were initially put into state childcare.The adults flew back to the UK and were arrested at the airport. Sara's father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool were found guilty of Sara's murder. Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison and Batool received a minimum of 33 years.Her uncle, Faisal Malik, was found guilty of causing or allowing her death and given a 16-year sentence.Sara had been hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in Woking, Surrey.In Pakistan, Sara's grandfather was given temporary custody of her siblings in October 2023. All but the youngest are now attending school in Pakistan, the grandfather has said.Speaking following Saturday's decision, their grandfather said "we will help them to return to a normal life"."Hardships can happen to any person at any time, at any place," he said, adding "we will move forward".Muhammed said that he speaks to his son Urfan once a week or every second week. "Not with the children, not regarding the case. Nothing else, just to ask about each other's well-being".When asked about allegations that he had helped hide the three adults, Muhammed said they had left soon after arriving in Jhelum and that at the time he had told them to return to the UK.The children's grandfather added that the siblings will keep their British passports and go back to the UK "when they reach the right age".The children were made wards of court in England, and Surrey County council had been trying to bring them back through the courts in Pakistan.Their grandfather has been fighting for them to stay with him. Surrey withdrew from the case in June, saying it had no ability to pursue the application in Pakistan, as English proceedings are coming to an end.A final decision on their guardianship had not been made in Pakistan's courts until Saturday.

schema.headline: Sara Sharif's grandfather granted guardianship of her siblings in Pakistan

title: Twelve killed in attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport
description: At least 12 people have been killed and 309 injured in an attack on an international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, local authorities say, days
body: At least 12 people have been killed and 309 injured in an attack on an international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, local authorities say, days after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have carried out similar strikes on the hub.The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said the victims were four Saudi and two Bangladeshi nationals, while Egypt, Jordan, Palestine, Sudan, Syria and the US each had one of their citizens killed. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh have been suspended.More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness. The US embassy said it was "aware of attacks", urging Americans to avoid the area.A projectile also fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam in eastern Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition which is fighting the Houthis said.The attack comes a day after authorities said three Saudis including a pilot were killed in two attacks on the airport by the Iran-backed Houthis the day prior. Another three people were killed in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October.An eyewitness who said they had been in the domestic terminal told the news agency that they had seen gate 401 hit and "injured [people] in front of my eyes", adding: "Everyone was running."Western embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens away from the airport, while the UK Foreign Office told British nationals to stay away "until the airport is secure and to monitor the advice of the Saudi authorities".Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there.All flights to Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled, aviation tracker Flightradar shows.Doctors had been asked to report to hospitals to address the situation, a medical source told AFP."We were told we are dealing with a 'serious emergency situation'," the medical source told the agency.The suspected attack comes during a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west.The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war.The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive.That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government.A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.But the informal truce began to unravel in July.The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on Sanaa airport.

schema.headline: Twelve killed in attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport

title: Ukraine war: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 20 people
description: Russia has attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 20 people including four children, local officials said
body: Russia has attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 20 people including four children, local officials said.The glide bombs hit residential buildings in the southern city on Saturday morning. At least 32 others were injured in the attack, with more still missing and believed to be under the rubble.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks on Zaporizhzhia were Russia expressing "its thanks" for a deal announced by US President Donald Trump last night easing sanctions on Moscow to import Russian diesel.He added that 13 other regions had come under attack overnight, arguing this demonstrated Russia took "any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting".Photos and videos from the site of one of the strikes in Zaporizhzhia show an apartment block mostly destroyed. "The ground floor was hit, and the floors above just collapsed," acting Mayor Regina Harchenko told Ukrainian television from the scene. She said more than 80 workers were involved in ongoing search and rescue operations which are expected to continue throughout the day. The rescuers regularly stop to listen for any noises made by survivors who could be under the rubble.Harchenko said Russia had struck at "our very heart" and "our littlest ones" were among those killed, adding that their deaths were "awful grief for their families. For the city."Zaporizhzhia is a major regional centre with more than 700,000 residents. It is located less than 10 miles (16km) from the front line and is frequently attacked by Russian drones and missiles.Zelensky was quick to criticise Trump's diesel deal with Russia, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Analysts view the deal as an attempt by the US president to allay domestic concerns about high fuel prices ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.Zelensky wrote on social media on Saturday that Russian attacks on energy facilities in the capital, Kyiv, demonstrated Russia's "true intentions"."Russia's choice is war. And they will be ready to end it only when they feel that their ability to drag the war out is diminishing."Unfortunately, the signals Russia received yesterday were entirely different – signals suggesting that it could simply keep attacking. And this needs to be corrected."Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks on infrastructure in recent months, as Moscow's full-scale invasion, launched in 2022, drags on.On Thursday, at least 33 people were killed in another Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in Kramatorsk, in the eastern Donetsk region. The day before, 22 people including five children died as a Russian missile hit an apartment block in the town of Pryluky, east of Kyiv.The number of civilian casualties in Ukraine jumped by 55%, external in the first eight months of this year, according to the UN.Russia has also stepped up its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure as winter approaches, a strategy it has undertaken in previous years. Kyiv has repeatedly accused it of targeting Ukraine's civilian population, which Moscow denies.For its part, Ukraine has increasingly adopted a policy of striking infrastructure often deep inside Russia that is crucial to its economy, including several oil refineries and terminals.Several strikes on data centres owned by Yandex have left the tech giant struggling to maintain services.Kyiv says its strikes are aimed at curtailing revenue streams for Russia's war machine.

schema.headline: Ukraine war: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 20 people

title: Green Party MP wants to make sure it is 'not vulnerable to extremists'
description: A Green Party MP has said her party needs to make sure it is not "vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists" after members voted for a motion th
body: A Green Party MP has said her party needs to make sure it is not "vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists" after members voted for a motion that claimed Zionism was racism. The motion put forward by activists, which became formal policy after it was approved at the Green's conference earlier this month, has divided senior party figures and been criticised by Jewish groups. Westminster leader Ellie Chowns told the BBC it was a "significant and damaging policy" and she would work to reform the Green Party. It comes after ex-leader Caroline Lucas said it was not being protected from entryism - where people sign up to a party to try to change it. Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today Programme on Saturday, Chowns said: "I don't know if there are extremists and racists in my party. But I want to make sure that my party isn't vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists."The MP described Zionism as a "contested concept" and said the motion did not represent the views of the large majority of Green Party members, "nor of people in the country". Chowns said the motion would be a "distraction from the very important work" the party has been doing campaigning for Palestinian rights.She added: "I think it is clear that if we have policy, such significant and damaging policy, made by a vote of just 0.4% of our members, that something isn't working in our structures and our policy-making process."Members of the Green Party of England and Wales endorsed the policy motion by 1,022 votes to 813.There are 230,000 members of the Green party overall and not everyone attended the conference.The policy also backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.It defines Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state".The Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council, which criticised the motion, said: "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it."Appearing on BBC Radio 4 programme Any Questions on Friday, Lucas said she was not putting any blame on the party's current leader, Zack Polanski, who she said had done "great things" for the party. "Our constitution was written decades ago, well before we had MPs, before we had mayors, before we had anything like the number of that we have today," the ex-leader said.Lucas, who was for years the face of the Greens as its first and sole MP until 2024, added the party needed to be made "a welcoming place for Jewish people."A Green Party spokesperson said: "Green Party membership has increased since Zack Polanksi announced his leadership bid in May 2025. Unlike other political parties, our members can bring and set policy."This is one motion alongside dozens of others that was discussed at our biggest-ever party conference. Every motion submitted to conference undergoes debate and no single interest group drives policy. "Polanski, who is Jewish, previously told the BBC he would not have voted for the motion and instead would have voted for an amended version.However, he said the "substantial part of the motion", that "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by a racist ideology" was "obvious".Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.Ashok Kumar, a Green Party member and part of the Greens for Palestine group, voted for the motion and told the BBC last week it was about "Palestinian liberation."He said he didn't feel the vote was harming the image of the Green Party, and that a growing number of people see this as a core issue. "They see the violence that's (been) occurring over the last three years," he told BBC Politics Live., external "So, I think the Zionist position is actually the marginal position.

schema.headline: Green Party MP wants to make sure it is 'not vulnerable to extremists'

title: Man dies after tiger attack at Yorkshire Wildlife Park
description: A man has died after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police have confirmed.South Yorkshire Police said it had been called at 13:
body: A man has died after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police have confirmed.South Yorkshire Police said it had been called at 13:35 BST to reports of a man entering the tiger enclosure at the attraction near Doncaster. The tiger then attacked the man and he died at the scene, the force said.His family had been informed and were being supported by officers, it added.A park spokesperson said: "We are deeply saddened by today's tragic incident. Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies are with the family and loved ones of the person who has lost their life."They added: "We are working closely with the police and relevant authorities and would ask that the privacy of those affected is respected at this extremely difficult time. The park will remain closed tomorrow."Police said the tiger was uninjured, remained in the enclosure following the incident and there had been no wider risk to the public.The park was evacuated and officers remain at the scene.The force added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage."Earlier, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened".

schema.headline: Man dies after tiger attack at Yorkshire Wildlife Park

title: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
description: Figure caption, Watch: Florida thrashed as Hurricane Isaias makes landfallByMadeline HalpertReporting fromNew YorkUpdated 1 hour agoFour people have d
body: Figure caption, Watch: Florida thrashed as Hurricane Isaias makes landfallByMadeline HalpertReporting fromNew YorkUpdated 1 hour agoFour people have died and hundreds of thousands are without power after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern US with powerful winds and heavy rain. Officials reported two deaths each in the states of Alabama and Florida, which included people who were killed when trees fell on their houses. At least 600,000 people were without power in several states as of Saturday afternoon, according to tracker PowerOutage. Isaias made landfall in Florida late on Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105mph (168km/h) before being downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone. The storm felled trees and ripped the roofs off buildings. Alabama, Florida and Georgia all declared states of emergency ahead of its arrival, while both Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders to thousands of people.Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon is bearing down on Mexico's Pacific coast and has strengthened to category four. It is expected to make landfall sometime overnight.And Tropical Storm Rachel, also in the Pacific Ocean, is edging towards land and is expected to hit southern California later on Saturday.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The roof was blown off an apartment complex in Milton, FloridaImage source, Getty ImagesTwo deaths related to Isaias were reported in Florida's Escambia County. A woman was killed when a tree fell on her house, local Sheriff Chip Simmons said. Joey Williams told NewsNation his wife had died in the storm. He said they went outside to snap pictures of the damage but, when they went back into their home, a tree fell through the roof and trapped them. "I was able to squeeze out. My wife didn't make it," Williams told the outlet. Simmons later reported that a man had died from carbon monoxide poisoning after running a generator in a garage that was not properly ventilated. Four other people who were in the same house were taken to hospital. Officials had to rescue people in vehicles that became submerged by floodwaters. The Florida National Guard shared pictures of a truck stuck in a flood ditch, saying soldiers "stopped, swam to the vehicle and pulled its occupants to safety".Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said flooding was a continued risk and warned of a "very hazardous situation". Image source, EPAImage caption, In Florida, the storm tore through housesImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The canopy of a petrol station collapsed in Gulf Breeze, FloridaIn neighbouring Alabama, a sheriff was injured when a tree fell on him as he was responding to a car crash. "Unfortunately, we have also learned that two Alabamians have lost their lives," Governor Kay Ivey said in a post on X, without giving further details on the circumstances of the deaths.She also said officials were concerned about "spinoff tornadoes" in the state from the strong winds and heavy rain. "As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop," she said.In Charleston, South Carolina, officials asked people to stay home on Saturday night as high tide is expected to reach 7.5ft (2.3m). "After dark, floodwater is much harder to see and it's impossible to judge how deep it is from behind the wheel," the city said. The storm is expected to continue to weaken as it travels to the north-east, but the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) warned that the Carolinas and Georgia could see floods from up to 10 inches (25cm) of rainfall. Hurricane Isaias was the first hurricane in the Atlantic's hurricane season, which largely has been delayed due to El Niño conditions in the Pacific.Image source, EPAImage caption, Residents have begun removing felled treesFigure caption, Watch: Powerful waves crash ashore as Hurricane Isaias approaches US

schema.headline: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US

title: The rock behind Chelsea's entertainers: Midfield duo key for Blues
description: Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson were paired in midfield for the first time as Chelsea produced their most complete performance of the season.In a
body: Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson were paired in midfield for the first time as Chelsea produced their most complete performance of the season.In a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth on Saturday, manager Xabi Alonso finally found the control and stability required behind his free-scoring attacking trio of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.The Blues have had no problems scoring goals this campaign, with 15 goals from six matches, but no team has conceded more than their total of 13.Against the Cherries though, Caicedo and Henderson provided the balance to suggest Alonso could finally have found an answer - despite still having to wait for their first clean sheet of the league campaign.Henderson stole the show by scoring his first two goals for the club. He opened the scoring with a curling effort after 66 seconds before adding a 25-yard free-kick to complete the victory.Having also set up Rogers for the second goal after just two minutes and 30 seconds, the 36-year-old became the third-oldest player to score and provide an assist in the same match for Chelsea, behind only Didier Drogba and Gianfranco Zola.Henderson's performance came after a shift in Chelsea's summer recruitment strategy. He arrived on a free transfer from Brentford to add experience to what had been the Premier League's youngest squad.Alonso said: "We signed him for everything. If he's able to score two beauties like today, we are more than happy for him."But apart from the goals, he's done many, many good things. I think today was a very complete performance. We were in control for most of the game, so I'm happy with that. We had good stability in defence as well."Having not signed a player aged over 30 since Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang in 2022, Chelsea recruited three this summer, with goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez joining from Aston Villa and striker Danny Welbeck also arriving.Now, recovered from a broken arm sustained while jumping over an advertising hoarding during celebrations following England's win over Mexico at the World Cup, Henderson is showing he is more than just a vocal leader behind the scenes.There is a strong argument that Chelsea find it easier to cope without the creativity of Cole Palmer than without Caicedo's ability in possession and his knack for breaking up play in midfield.In his 150th appearance for the club, Caicedo lasted 72 minutes. His withdrawal for Romeo Lavia was planned, but the Ecuador international still made a significant impact.Alonso deployed him in a deep role, dropping into the middle of the back three when Chelsea were in possession and allowing young defender Josh Acheampong to push forward.He misplaced just two passes and recorded the highest pass-completion rate of any Chelsea starter. He also made and won more tackles than any other Chelsea player on Saturday afternoon. With Caicedo in the side, Chelsea have won 48.1% of their Premier League matches. Without him, that figure drops to 25%.Alonso said: "You always want to have Moises on the pitch. With him, we have a better midfield area and when you are better in the middle, you have a more complete team. "I think that is something to build around. With the players that we have up front, they are solid in defence as well. So, I'm happy that Moises is feeling better because he's going to be a key player for us. We knew that."The alternative options in Chelsea's midfield include captain Reece James, who is able to play in defence, along with substitutes Romeo Lavia and Valentin Barco, who did not make the matchday squad. It is most likely James who will be attempting to re-take his place from Henderson when back, but the diagnosis on his knee issues remains uncertain.Chelsea remain a work in progress and conceded again through poor set-piece defending for Evanilson's goal.However, if Henderson and Caicedo can help eliminate the defensive lapses, Chelsea can begin to look up the table, with Pedro, Rogers and Palmer already helping to make them the Premier League's top scorers.Alonso said: "I think that they help each other well and they give presence, they give stability. "You know that they are going to be the ones that are going to be helping the rest, not just for their qualities because they understand the game. They can play in shorter spaces but as well defensively they give good balance."Former England striker Alan Shearer told BBC Sport: "Caicedo makes a difference. There's no doubt about it. He gives Chelsea a bit more solidity and stops the ball getting into the back four."He and Henderson have worked really well, the opening goal being a good example. He definitely makes them more solid, I've been really impressed."

schema.headline: The rock behind Chelsea's entertainers: Midfield duo key for Blues

title: Northern Lights: Aurora stun UK down to England's south coast
description: Image source, BBC Weather Watchers / Jonny GiosImage caption, Kendal in Cumbria paid host to the breathtaking scenes on SaturdayResidents across the U
body: Image source, BBC Weather Watchers / Jonny GiosImage caption, Kendal in Cumbria paid host to the breathtaking scenes on SaturdayResidents across the UK were left stunned as the sky was illuminated by the spectacular colours of the Northern Lights on Friday and Saturday evenings.The natural phenomenon, known as the Aurora Borealis, is the result of increased solar activity.Such occurrences are mostly visible near the Arctic Circle and northern Scotland, but particularly strong activity levels meant they could be seen as far south as Devon, Hampshire and Kent on Saturday night.The Met Office has said sightings could continue to be possible during clear skies until Tuesday.Image source, BBC Weather Watchers / Simon Luckman 1988Image caption, The phenomenon was visible as a pink haze in Winterton-on-Sea, Norfolk, on FridayImage source, BBC Weather Watchers / Isle ExplorerImage caption, Owston Ferry in North Lincolnshire was graced by a stunning purple haze Image source, BBC Weather Watchers /ChelseaPhilImage caption, Sightings stretched to Herne Bay in Kent Northern Lights are caused by powerful solar eruptions from the Sun, called coronal mass ejections (CMEs).Towards the end of last week, the Sun was observed to unleash CMEs directed towards the Earth.This stream of charged particles can get captured by the Earth's magnetic field and directed into our atmosphere, especially towards polar regions.When these charged particles collide with oxygen and nitrogen, photons of coloured light are emitted - this is the aurora.Image source, BBC Weather Watchers / Sarah n EssieImage caption, Revellers were able to take in a mix of green and purple in Saltburn-by-the-Sea, Redcar and Cleveland Image source, BBC Weather Watchers / HolImage caption, Stenness on Scotland's Orkney Islands served as a strong location for the phenomenonImage source, BBC Weather Watchers / Hannah and BenImage caption, The sky was illuminated in Holmwood, SurreyThe chances of seeing the aurora vary across the UK depending upon its strength. When activity levels reach 200nT (nanotesla) the aurora would be visible in the north of the UK, but not the south.On Saturday evening, those levels reached 600nT, meaning it would be visible across the whole of the UK, even in the south, which is a much rarer phenomenon.Experts have previously said 2026 will be a peak year for aurora-spotting as the Sun has been in a heightened state of activity as part of its 11-year natural cycle.Image source, BBC Weather Watchers / Carolyn RImage caption, A purple glow could be seen across the sky in Salisbury, Wiltshire on SaturdayImage source, BBC Weather Watchers / Rick1Image caption, North Yorkshire did not miss out on the action, as shown here in ScarboroughImage source, BBC Weather Watchers / RockdodgerImage caption, An array of pink, blue and green could be seen in Gourock, InverclydeIf you missed out this time, the aurora may return on Sunday.The Met Office has said sightings remain possible across Scotland and similar geomagnetic longitudes during clear skies until Tuesday.To see them, you need to look northwards, away from bright streetlights, and look through a mobile phone camera.The reason you need to use a camera is because in low-light conditions at night our eyes use rod cells to see - these cells do not perceive colour and so we actually see in black and white. Cameras do not have the same limitations.

schema.headline: Northern Lights: Aurora stun UK down to England's south coast

title: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago - why are they resuming now?
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, An estimated crowd of 20,000 gathered in Kentucky in 1936 for the public hanging of Rainey BetheaBySheila Fly
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, An estimated crowd of 20,000 gathered in Kentucky in 1936 for the public hanging of Rainey BetheaBySheila FlynnSenior US reporterUpdated 10:17 BSTThey came in their thousands from near and far. Men, women and children lined up on a Kentucky riverfront for the public hanging of a black man convicted of raping and killing an elderly white widow.It was 14 August 1936 in Owensboro, Kentucky, a sweltering Friday in the middle of a legendary heatwave. Some slept overnight near the gallows to preserve their spots. Others held "necktie" parties the previous evening, arriving hungover as teenagers sold popcorn and soda to spectators.By the execution time of 05:00, the crowd had swelled to an estimated 20,000.That's when Rainey Bethea, an orphan in his 20s, stepped up to the gallows - sentenced to death after allegedly confessing to robbing, raping and killing Lischia Edwards, 70.The previous afternoon, he'd eaten a last meal of fried chicken, pork chops, mashed potatoes, pickled cucumbers, cornbread, lemon pie and ice cream.Many of those gathered - including press from as far away as Chicago and New York - came to see the rumoured "Lady Executioner". The local sheriff had died four months earlier and his widow had become his unlikely replacement. She declined to pull the trip lever herself, however, and it was a hired hangmen who instead sent Bethea to his death.That moment marked the last high-profile public hanging in the US. The circus surrounding Bethea's death embarrassed many in Kentucky and the governor outlawed public executions 18 months later.By then, most states had abolished capital punishment in view of the masses as societal attitudes sought more humane and private methods. Another hanging was attended by a few hundred in Missouri in 1937, but that was lesser known and marked America's final public execution - until now.Image source, FPG/Staff/GettyImage caption, Men, women and children attended the hanging, which marked the last high-profile public execution in the USA little more than 90 years after Bethea's killing, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced that the military would publicly execute Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 unarmed fellow soldiers in 2009 at the Fort Hood military base in Texas.The Pentagon followed up by saying the execution by firing squad in December would be livestreamed."People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said.University of Colorado professor emeritus Michael Radelet, a long-time scholar of capital punishment, was shocked."I never imagined [another] public execution," he told the BBC.He noted how public support for the death penalty in general has been steadily declining - it was at 80% in 1994, for example, but now stands at 52%."It's gone down precipitously, especially when you give the alternative of life without parole," he said.It's too soon to know what the American public thinks of the idea of livestreaming an execution. But it's likely that millions or more will tune in.With Hegseth's announcement, Radelet said, "the justification for the death penalty becomes entertainment... bring your popcorn, invite your friends". Figure caption, Americans discuss their views on the death penalty after the botched execution in Tennessee of convicted murderer Christa PikeSonya Lea, who just last year published a book about Bethea's execution, "felt absolute horror for our descendants" when she heard of the announced firing squad livestream."What they called it in 1936 was a carnival of sadism," she said. "That we now have the technology that can make it go wider than the 20,000 people who showed up... to witness in Owensboro, Kentucky, it just makes it even more horrific."Lea's grandparents were teenage newlyweds among that 1936 crowd. She only found out after her grandmother's death in 2002, when she read an account her late grandma had given detailing how they were close enough to hear Bethea's neck snap.The author's subsequent years of research taught her that many Kentuckians were "haunted" by that execution."I really thought, with all my heart, that we had put this in the rearview mirror, this level of grotesquery that only a few countries in the world engage in - Iran, North Korea, Afghanistan," she said. "Are we now, as the United States of America, considering ourselves to be part of that kind of government? It's just horrific."But the polarisation and rhetoric in US politics may have set the stage for such an announcement, said Kurt Gray, a social psychology professor at Ohio State University."Some Americans might thirst for blood, but I think a lot of Americans don't and, if anything, I think a lot of other Americans are just kind of maybe desensitised," he said. "So it's not like they're cheering a public execution - they're just like, 'Oh, yeah, I guess that's where we're at now.'"Figure caption, Can the Fort Hood shooter’s execution be livestreamed?Other research indicates that Hegseth and the administration may be reading the country wrong.Garen Wintemute, director of the Violence Prevention Research Program at the University of California, Berkeley, said surveys point to a declining appetite for violence in the US."This morning, the chair of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops labelled this [livestream execution announcement] as barbaric," he said. "And I think he speaks for a lot of people.""I think it's this: a public execution is not who we are," he added. "It's not who we aspire to be as a country."The debate over Hegseth's surprise announcement appeared to be playing out within the White House on Friday. US Vice-President JD Vance expressed uncertainty to reporters about whether the public execution would go ahead as planned and said he would not watch it if it were livestreamed.Hours later, US President Donald Trump said he "absolutely" approved of the livestream plan but that the Pentagon was still "making a determination" on it.He did not answer the question of whether he'd watch Hasan's execution. "I really don't care how he goes as long as he goes," Trump said. "And I think that the death penalty is a very worthy way of going for him."

schema.headline: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago - why are they resuming now?

title: 'I kissed Rodrigo' - Roberto de Zerbi praises Bentancur's red card against Manchester United
description: Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi praised Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in the 1-1 draw against Manchester United.The Uruguay midfielder was s
body: Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi praised Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in the 1-1 draw against Manchester United.The Uruguay midfielder was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a feisty 78th-minute melee when Spurs were trailing 1-0 at Old Trafford.Despite being reduced to 10 men, Tottenham managed to salvage a point as Dominic Solanke headed home in the second minute of added time.Spurs remain winless in the Premier League this season after six games, but De Zerbi was thankful to Bentancur for providing a "spark" against United. "I kiss Rodrigo and say thanks," De Zerbi said in his post-match press conference."In that moment maybe with 10 players we played with more courage, more energy."For a long time Tottenham played without this blood, this character."The incident happened when Shaw, on the receiving end of a reckless challenge by Bentancur, raced towards the Spurs player and shoved him off the pitch.Bentancur reacted by planting his head towards Shaw's face. The pair were separated by their team-mates before referee Stuart Attwell sent the substitute off.De Zerbi said it was a "mistake" by Bentancur, but added it was the type of reaction Tottenham needed to finish the game."I kissed Bentancur in the dressing room because we need this type of reaction, this character. Football is character," he told Sky Sports."I liked the situation with the red card. We need at this moment the situation, not to bring a red card but we need to not accept the defeat."Despite the late elation sparked by Solanke's 92nd-minute equaliser, Tottenham remain in the relegation zone with just three points from their opening six matches.It is just the fourth time the club have failed to win each of their opening six games of a league season, after 2008-09, 1955-56 and 1912-13.Spurs have often looked lively in attack this season, but they have lacked conviction in front of goal and only 19th-placed Coventry have scored fewer goals than Tottenham's three.However, Tottenham fans can take belief from their overall performance at Old Trafford as they ran United ragged in the opening half with fluid, high-tempo football."Today has been the game where for the first time this season we showed we are a team," De Zerbi said."We played for the team-mates, we played together, we stayed inside of the game in every situation and we attacked as a team and defended as a team."The Italian manager added on Sky Sports: "I'm very happy because I've seen the right spirit, the right character and I want to start from this character, this reaction, this behaviour."Tottenham spent more than £250m on new talent over the summer - adding 10 players to their squad.But their poor start has prompted the club to organise a warm-weather training camp in Spain, with the team expected to travel to Marbella on Sunday in the hope it will provide a chance for their new-look squad to bond."Now the target is to build the team," De Zerbi said. "We are a great group of players but we are not a team yet and to be a team is to play for the team-mates, suffer together, attack together."Spurs face newly-promoted Coventry on Monday, 19 October before making the short trip to Chelsea the following Saturday.

schema.headline: 'I kissed Rodrigo' - Roberto de Zerbi praises Bentancur's red card against Manchester United

title: Arsenal 2-1 Leeds: A decisive moment of real quality - but Mikel Arteta still has issues to address
description: Hincapie injury adds to Arsenal issues after Guimaraes rescue actFigure caption, Highlights: Arsenal survive scare to come from behind to beat LeedsFo
body: Hincapie injury adds to Arsenal issues after Guimaraes rescue actFigure caption, Highlights: Arsenal survive scare to come from behind to beat LeedsFor the second time in three Premier League matches, Bruno Guimaraes has come to Arsenal's rescue.Having sparked their 2-0 win at Sunderland in September with the crucial first goal, the £75m summer signing came off the bench again to have a pivotal impact against Leeds on Saturday.This time it was the winner as the Gunners came from behind for a 2-1 success in a testing encounter at Emirates Stadium.But Ecuador international Piero Hincapie was carried off during the warm-down, raising concern the defender has suffered an injury.He came on as a late substitute against Daniel Farke's side but completed extra running after the final whistle - a practice most clubs use.A fifth win in six league games put Mikel Arteta's side level on points with leaders Manchester City, but their title defence has certainly not been without its scares so far.Following on from their comprehensive 3-0 defeat at Brighton last time out, Arsenal fell behind in a league match for a third time in four league matches - and only a David Raya penalty save stopped them from trailing at Sunderland as well.For large parts of the game against Leeds, they were nowhere near their best but, after going behind in the 55th minute, Riccardo Calafiori and Guimaraes - on his full home debut - secured an important three points. "It was a great game of football. Leeds were brilliant for one hour." said Ally McCoist on TNT Sports. "Mikel Arteta made changes when he needed to and the substitutions gave Arsenal what they needed. That's what champions do. Leeds can hold their heads high." By getting wins when below par the mark of champions or are there reasons for concern for Arteta and Arsenal?Figure caption, Mikel Arteta post match interview - Arsenal vs Leeds UnitedGuimaraes raises level after Brighton woeComing into the season as defending champions, Arsenal were looking to make a statement signing to make their rivals take notice. They did not bring in the attacker they wanted but Guimaraes looks like he could be that key arrival to help Arteta's men build on their success. The 28-year-old midfielder is a 'win-now' signing in the peak years of his career. He responded well to a disappointing performance in the defeat by Brighton, where he made his full league debut.The Brazilian international has now scored two goals that have helped his side to valuable points and justified the decision to spend big on Guimaraes, even if the Gunners are inundated with top quality options in midfield. Arteta said: "He wasn't at that level against Brighton, and this is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action, you have to be at that level."Today was much better. That's what we have to demand, and this is what I demand to myself. I'm going to demand the same with the players, because if we do that, he will raise the standards and we will be a better team."Guimaraes was the first player to score twice from the bench this season and both goals have been from outside the box.Figure caption, Guimaraes has 'perfect' day despite jet lag'The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing'Arsenal won the league last season in part because of their excellent defence. The Gunners conceded the fewest goals in the league but have already conceded five in six games. The partnership of Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba is one of the best in the world and Arsenal look to be missing the injured Frenchman's calmness. Ezri Konsa was brought in from Aston Villa for £55m and, despite his quality, is still getting used to his new surroundings.It is unclear how serious Hincapie's injury is, although he was seen clutching his right ankle as he was carried off by goalkeeper Illan Meslier.He signed for the club on a permanent deal this summer, having initially joined on loan from Bayer Leverkusen last season.Hincapie has suffered from muscular issues this term and now faces an anxious wait to discover whether he requires another spell on the sidelines.Left-back Calafiori, though, has proved integral to Arsenal's attacking threat. His equaliser against Leeds was his first league strike this term but no defender has been involved in more Premier League goals than the Italian (one goal, two assists). "The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing." added Arteta. "And we need to be very conscious of that. From being exceptional and being the champions to being extremely average, like in that game, is a really thin line. "So if you don't want it more than the opponent, you are not able to cope emotionally with certain situations, you're going to suffer. "And we all suffered and we didn't enjoy that game, but then you have to learn the lesson and we certainly done that. "We speak about it and you could sense that there was something in those tummies."Madueke gets chance after attacking strugglesArteta made some big calls when naming his starting XI. He opted to start with German Kai Havertz up front despite the forward returning early from international duty after picking up a hamstring issue, leaving Viktor Gyokeres on the bench again. Gyokeres had scored four goals, registering in every match for Sweden, in the last international break, but looks to have work to do to win his manager round. The 28-year-old has yet to start a Premier League game and in his cameos this season has looked far from the level required as a striker who could fire Arsenal to back-to-back titles. The forward line did not click against Leeds and, with Havertz looking like he lacked match sharpness, thoughts turned towards whether Arsenal missing out on an elite attacker in the summer would haunt them. Winger Christos Tzolis, who has shone at times this season following his summer arrival, suffered a hamstring issue with Greece and, with Eberechi Eze out of form, Arteta used Noni Madueke on the left wing. Madueke was left out of the last England squad due to a lack of minutes with Arsenal but, after "being the best player in training for the last 10 days" according to Arteta, now could be the chance for him to prove his worth.

schema.headline: Arsenal 2-1 Leeds: A decisive moment of real quality - but Mikel Arteta still has issues to address

title: The Prem: Northampton 71-48 Bath: Saints score 11 tries to beat Bath in try-fest
description: The PremNorthampton (26) 71Tries: F Smith, Sleightholme 3, Freeman 2, Dingwall, Pater, Kemeny, Mitchell, Coles Cons: F Smith 8 Bath (29) 48Tries: Carr
body: The PremNorthampton (26) 71Tries: F Smith, Sleightholme 3, Freeman 2, Dingwall, Pater, Kemeny, Mitchell, Coles Cons: F Smith 8 Bath (29) 48Tries: Carr-Smith, C Griffin, A Griffin, Green 2, Carreras, Bayliss Cons: Russell 5 Pens: RussellNorthampton came out on top of a high-octane 18-try thriller at home to Bath, the second highest scoring game in English top-flight history.The two sides had surpassed 100 points on the scoreboard with 15 minutes remaining and continued to showcase unstoppable, attacking flair as the play went end-to-end.Northampton eventually streaked clear in the second half, with Ollie Sleightholme scoring a hat-trick and Tommy Freeman scoring twice as they finished with 11 tries and bounced back from defeat by Bristol a week ago.The loss is the first of the season for Bath, who made 12 changes for the match, with Arthur Green getting two of their seven tries and Charlie Griffin also scoring one on his Prem debut.The 119 points scored falls short of the record in the English top flight - the 127 points shared in Saints' 94-33 win over Bristol in May.Northampton Saints head coach Sam Vesty told BBC Radio Northampton:"Both teams took opportunities pretty quickly and I think both teams will be slightly disappointed in how they exited their end, in terms of when they've got the ball and got control of it."We gave it up quite a lot to them and put ourselves defensively under pressure  We're not happy with the 48 part of that scoreline. "We don't want it to be basketball. Obviously lots and lots of very good stuff but there's a good couple of areas for us to focus to be better - a more ruthless Bath and that's a very different game.[On the attack] "We were so clinical with our execution of what we were doing. Absolutely fantastic. "I thought our breakdown was very good, lots and lots of positives but we need to be better coming out of our end."Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan told BBC Radio Bristol:"It's dsappointing if you score 48 points away from home and lose the game."I think we lost control between minutes 50 and 60. The back end of both halves we conceded a yellow card and against a team like Saints it's difficult to contain them."But look at the positives, we played some fantastic rugby today."Northampton: Pater; Freeman, Hutchinson, Dingwall (c), Sleightholme; Smith, Mitchell; Iyogun, Langdon, Kundiona; Coles, Van Der Mescht, Kemeny, Pollock, Chick.Replacements: Smith, Fischetti, Neculai, Lockett, Prowse, Taylor, McParland, Belleau.Bath: Carreras; Cokanasiga, Ojomoh, Redpath, C. Griffin; Russell, Carr-Smith; Kirk, Tuipulotu, A. Griffin; Jeanes, Molony, Bayliss, Reid (c), Green.Replacements: Dunn, Obano, Stuart, Ewels, Hill, Davies, Lawrence, Coetzee.Sin bin: Bayliss (26) Lawrence (62)Referee: Matthew Carley

title: We shot the last film to be made in 'Scotland's Chornobyl'
description: Scotland's 'Chornobyl' housing scheme takes starring role in new horror filmImage source, BehindImage caption, Jade McDonald in a scene in Alessio Ave
body: Scotland's 'Chornobyl' housing scheme takes starring role in new horror filmImage source, BehindImage caption, Jade McDonald in a scene in Alessio Avezzano's sci-fi horror comedy Behind  BySteven McKenzieBBC Scotland NewsUpdated 6 October 2026A short film has captured some of the last images of a derelict housing estate nicknamed "Scotland's Chornobyl" before demolition crews moved in.The tenements at Clune Park in Port Glasgow were built a century ago as housing for shipyard workers but most of the buildings lay empty for years.Glasgow-based filmmaker Alessio Avezzano shot scenes for his post-apocalyptic sci-fi horror comedy, Behind, on the estate before bulldozers moved in last May."It's the last film to be made there. It was announced it would be demolished the day we were filming - we managed to get in there not a moment too soon," said the Scottish-Italian writer and director.Image source, BehindImage caption, Scenes for Behind were shot on the day it was announced Clune Park would be demolishedRedevelopment of Clune Park had been delayed for years due to a stand-off between private landlords and the local council, leaving the site frozen in time with just a handful of tenants remaining.Large parts of the site became run-down and comparisons were made with the Ukrainian city of Pripyat, abandoned after the 1986 explosion at the Chornobyl nuclear plant led to a huge radiation leak.Figure caption, Watch: BBC Scotland News footage of Clune Park before demolition teams moved in last yearThe plot for Behind was inspired by "butt dialling", accidentally calling someone from a phone placed in a back pocket.In the film, it has devastating consequences.Avezzano said he come up with the idea while trying to write a script."That week my cousin, who hadn't done this before or since, just started to butt dial me every day and by the fifth day the light bulb moment came," he said."It is basically taking the idea of butt dials and what if they were a symptom of something more deadly."Avezzano added: "It's got elements of how we responded to the pandemic and it's got elements of phone addiction and social media addiction.""It's post-apocalyptic satire."Image source, BehindImage caption, Avezzano said he was fascinated by the estateImage source, BehindImage caption, The short has been taken on a tour of film festivalsAvezzano said Clune Park gave him the ideal backdrop for the short, and scenes were shot in areas accessible to the public.Scenes for 2013's sci-fi horror Under the Skin, starring Scarlett Johansson, were also filmed at the estate."The idea it was described as Scotland's Chornobyl has always been fascinating." said Avezzano, who is working on his first feature - Midgies - a horror film set in Scotland and due to be released next year.This YouTube post cannot be displayed in your browser. Please enable Javascript or try a different browser.View original content on YouTubeThe BBC is not responsible for the content of external sites. YouTube content may contain adverts.Skip youtube video by Mythic PicnicAllow YouTube content?This article contains content provided by Google YouTube. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. You may want to read Google’s cookie policy, external and privacy policy, external before accepting. To view this content choose ‘accept and continue’.The BBC is not responsible for the content of external sites. YouTube content may contain adverts.The film was entirely self-funded.The lead character is played by Jade McDonald who was in the female run of Singin' I'm No a Billy He's a Tim, a play about a Celtic fan and a Rangers fan locked in a prison cell together on the day of an Old Firm match.Behind has been taken on a tour of international film festivals, including in Italy and Argentina, following its premiere at Glasgow Film Festival's Frightfest.It was nominated for the best editing prize at Basingstoke's Exit 6 Film Festival and won best international short at Roswell Shorts Festival in New Mexico. title: Manchester United: Another failure to beat 10 men increases pressure on boss Carrick
description: For the second time in successive home Premier League games, Manchester United failed to beat opponents reduced to 10 men.For the third time in as man
body: For the second time in successive home Premier League games, Manchester United failed to beat opponents reduced to 10 men.For the third time in as many seasons, a United manager finds himself under severe pressure before the clocks have gone back.Four weeks ago, Manchester City needed an incorrect video assistant referee (VAR) decision to take advantage of an ineffective United performance after Phil Foden had been shown a red card in the 23rd minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.On Saturday, the damage was self-inflicted as a Spurs side, who had given every indication of being unable to score before Rodrigo Bentancur's headfirst charge at Luke Shaw just five minutes after Bryan Mbeumo's opener, came up with an injury-time equaliser.Centre-back Lisandro Martinez was outmuscled embarrassingly easily by Dominic Solanke, with goalkeeper Senne Lammens failing to read the striker's deft touch that crept in at the far corner.The anguish on United faces told its own story."A worrying day for Michael Carrick," observed former United skipper Gary Neville on Sky Sports."I'm not happy with he amount of points we've got so far, for sure, you know," said Carrick."I'm not hiding, there's no hiding from that. I think it could have been different for a couple of little things here or there, but the reality is the reality, we've got to accept it, you know. We need to put things in a direction, in a positive direction quite quickly, that's pretty plain."The 'little things' Carrick talks about are the defending for Solanke's goal, the lack of pressure put on Everton's Ainsley Maitland-Niles when he smashed another injury-time equaliser at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on 6 September, and the preventable Martinez own goal that nearly gave Fulham victory at Craven Cottage just before the international break."We've got to be a little bit more streetwise in moments, a little bit more stubborn and a little bit stronger in seeing out certain things," he added."It doesn't change my belief or the confidence in the players, you know. We're a really good team and capable of being a really good team, but we've obviously got to start getting more points on the board, that's for sure."The problem is with each disappointment, the belief of United being 'a really good team' starts to ebb away.Yet again, a post-match focus centred on how much Carrick's team ran, even though running for the sake of it has proved to be of little benefit."The stats don't lie when every time the other team runs more than you," said Sky Sports pundit and former Spurs captain Jamie Redknapp."Tottenham ran 5km more than Man United. OK, they had 10 men but that is every game. If you outrun your opposing number, you will win games. I'm not saying they are not trying. It is that physical battle they are losing though."While, ex-Spurs midfielder Danny Murphy, added on BBC Match of the Day: "There was a lethargy about Man Utd, this midfield can't control games. It is partly tactical and partly personnel. "I don't understand it. We saw at the end of last season Man Utd were much  more organised and much more difficult to play against."The space in midfield was incredible and if they were playing against a more competent side, they would have been beaten. Play like that against good teams and they will be cut wide open."It feels as though some fans are losing faith already, judging by the way they reacted at moments during the game, aside from the boos that accompanied the end of each half.Forward Matheus Cunha - one of a number of Carrick's squad who have failed to reproduce the form he showed in the second half of last season - gestured to the crowd during the opening period. It wasn't clear whether he was responding to a negative comment or urging more noise, but the Brazilian clearly wasn't happy.Carrick's family are season ticket holders. He knows what it is like to watch United struggle at Old Trafford."Obviously, it hurts," he said. "It hurts a lot. It's not nice to go through. I care as much as anybody about this place. Sometimes you could say too much because then it overspills. But it's coming from a good place, really, and so I understand it."It is in moments like this that Carrick, who presents such a calm front in public, must be churning inside.He knows how the pressure can mount around Old Trafford and how fierce the debate around the club in the search for answers can be.As he said, Carrick cares. And he is certain his players feel the same."I don't feel let down," he added. "You can make mistakes."We've all got standards; we've all got levels. The players hold their hands up at times when something goes against them."It's not like everyone walks off into the distance tonight like everything's fine and it's left on me. It's not that at all. The players care, for sure."I don't feel let down by them for making a mistake. We've just got to all help each other be better, and it's on me to help them and guide them through it."

schema.headline: Manchester United: Another failure to beat 10 men increases pressure on boss Carrick
